body: Flag: POOR. Hyderabad infrastructure group that controlled Mumbai International Airport (MIAL, 50.5%) and Bangalore airport, plus power and roads, carrying group debt reported around Rs 32,000 cr (mid-2010s). Sold Bangalore airport stakes to Fairfax (33% in 2016, residual 10% for ~Rs 1,290 cr in 2017) to service debt -- the crown jewels went to lenders' needs rather than to shareholders. Allegations: CBI registered a case (27-Jun-2020) against chairman GVK Reddy, son G.V. Sanjay Reddy, MIAL and others alleging ~Rs 705 cr siphoned from MIAL -- ~Rs 310 cr via bogus works contracts with nine companies (2017-18) and ~Rs 395 cr of MIAL's surplus funds used for group companies (2012-2017); ED followed with a PMLA case. These are FIR allegations; no conviction or final finding was found in this scan. In 2020-21 Adani took control of MIAL by acquiring GVK's stake and debt; GVK Power & Infrastructure's listed shares became a penny stock. Early signals: holdco debt far above holdco cash flow, airport SPV surpluses moving to group companies, stake sales of the best assets, auditor qualifications on going concern. Lesson: when a group's only cash-generating asset is a regulated SPV with outside partners (AAI, ACSA, Bidvest), watch the SPV's related-party contracts.

data.status_2026: no current status found; MIAL with Adani; GVKPIL penny stock
